relevance_note: Case series of three children with arterial tortuosity syndrome and homozygous SLC2A10 variants: "we report 3 pediatric patients with homozygous SLC2A10 pathogenic variants".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON built with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans, then every span checked verbatim against the paper. Labels 'Case 1'-'Case 3' are the paper's own headings (Table 1 has patients as columns with headers Case 1, Case 2, Case 3). No variant description (cDNA/protein) is printed for any patient, so each variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'; zygosity 'homozygous' and pathogenicity 'pathogenic' come from each case's own sentence. Consanguinity and parental testing are not stated. Case 1 is identified as 'the neonatal patient'/'a neonate' in the abstract and summary; those statements were attributed to Case 1. Aneurysm and dissection for Case 3 (and dissection for Case 2) are excluded from the abstract statement about 'these cases' ('without aneurysm formation, dissection, or significant obstruction'), recorded as inferred from group statement; 'significant obstruction' was not used to exclude stenosis checklist items (narrower than stenosis). Aortic stenosis excluded for Case 2 and aortic arch obstruction excluded for Case 1 do not exclude the broader checklist item 'stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches', left not reported. Case 2 pulmonary arteries: mild flow turbulence (gradient 14 mmHg) is neither called stenosis nor excluded as such; pulmonary artery stenosis left not reported. Case 1 has 'mild dilation of the ascending aorta' but the paper states 'without evidence of aneurysm'; aortic root aneurysm checklist recorded excluded. Possible internal tension for Case 2: echocardiography reports 'normal ventricular size and function' while the Fig. 3 legend reports 'Global cardiomegaly with marked enlargement of the left side of the heart' and the referral/Table 1 give left ventricular hypertrophy; both feature rows (ventricular dilatation excluded, cardiomegaly observed) are emitted; the ventricular hypertrophy checklist item is recorded observed since no statement says hypertrophy is absent. Case 3 'bulging sternum (pectus deformity)' recorded as pectus excavatum or carinatum observed. Not given rows: Case 1's two cousins with congenital heart disease (family history only, not described as having ATS or tested) and Case 2's diabetic mother (not affected or tested); 'evaluation of bronchiolitis' and 'suspected congenital heart disease' (referral reasons, not confirmed findings) were not recorded as features. Ages: Case 2 and Case 3 ages at the evaluation described (15 months, 6 months) recorded as age at last evaluation; Case 1's later follow-up age is not stated, so last evaluation left not reported; age at diagnosis not stated for anyone.
